s0101.literal: When the Founder ascended the throne, [Ke] was appointed Administrator of Wuxing.
s0101.idiomatic: When the Founder took the throne, Ke was made administrator of Wuxing.

s0102.literal: In the second year of Yongding he was transferred to supervise Kuaiji commandery.
s0102.idiomatic: In Yongding year two he was transferred to oversee Kuaiji commandery.

s0103.literal: When Yu Xiaoshuo plotted to join Wang Lin, he sent troops from Linchuan to attack Zhou Di; Ke was made Stalwart-Martial General and led troops across the ranges to rescue Di.
s0103.idiomatic: When Yu Xiaoshuo plotted to side with Wang Lin and marched from Linchuan against Zhou Di, Ke was made stalwart-martial general and led an army over the mountains to relieve Di.

s0104.literal: When Yu Xiaoshuo heard Ke had arrived, he withdrew.
s0104.idiomatic: When Yu Xiaoshuo learned Ke was coming, he retreated.

s0105.literal: In year three he was transferred to Bearer of the Staff, Courier Scattered-Cavalry Regular Attendant, Intelligent-Martial General, and Inspector of Wu prefecture, and went by convenient route to Poyang.
s0105.idiomatic: In year three he was made bearer of the staff, courier scattered-cavalry regular attendant, intelligent-martial general, and inspector of Wu prefecture, and went by convenient route to Poyang.

s0106.literal: Soon there was an edict recalling him; he acted in Kuaiji commandery affairs.
s0106.idiomatic: Before long an edict recalled him, and he administered Kuaiji commandery affairs.

s0107.literal: That year he was appointed Scattered-Cavalry Regular Attendant, Loyal-Martial General, and Administrator of Kuaiji.
s0107.idiomatic: That year he was made scattered-cavalry regular attendant, loyal-martial general, and administrator of Kuaiji.

s0108.literal: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, [Ke] was additionally made Scattered-Cavalry Regular Attendant, Area Commander over Military Affairs in the eighteen prefectures of Guang, Heng, Eastern Heng, Jiao, Yue, Cheng, Ding, Xin, He, Luo, Ai, De, Yi, Huang, Li, An, Shi, and Shuang, General Who Guards the South, General Who Pacifies the Yue, and Inspector of Guangzhou.
s0108.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, Ke was further made scattered-cavalry regular attendant, commander of armies in eighteen southern provinces including Guang, Heng, Eastern Heng, Jiao, Yue, Cheng, Ding, Xin, He, Luo, Ai, De, Yi, Huang, Li, An, Shi, and Shuang, general who guards the south, general who pacifies the Yue, and inspector of Guangzhou.

s0109.literal: Before Ke reached the ranges, the former inspector Ouyang Xie raised troops blocking the passes; Ke could not advance. The court sent Minister of Works Zhang Zhaoda to command the armies to campaign against Xie; when Xie was pacified, [Ke] was able to enter the prefecture.
s0109.idiomatic: Before Ke crossed the mountains, the former inspector Ouyang Xie held the passes with an army and blocked him. The court sent Zhang Zhaoda, minister of works, to lead the armies against Xie; only after Xie was suppressed could Ke enter the province.

s0110.literal: The prefecture had suffered war and devastation; everywhere was ruined. Ke soothed and settled the people, covering them with kindness; the region beyond the ranges relied on him.
s0110.idiomatic: The province had been ravaged by war and lay in ruins. Ke comforted and settled the people, treating them with kindness, and the far south came to rely on him.

s0111.literal: The historiographer says: Hu Ying, Xu Du, Du Leng, and Shen Ke all attached to swift steeds and leaped upward, relied on the brilliance of sun and moon, first beheld the talent of royal assistants, then understood the measure of chief ministers; in life they ate at meat tables, in death they were granted temple shares.
s0111.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Hu Ying, Xu Du, Du Leng, and Shen Ke all rode swift steeds to rise, drew on the light of sun and moon, first saw the gifts of royal counselors, then grasped the stature of chief ministers; in life they feasted at court, in death they shared offerings in the ancestral temple.

s0114.literal: At Dongguan [they] inflicted a great defeat on them
s0114.idiomatic: At Dongguan they inflicted a great defeat on them

s0116.literal: Deleted according to the Northern Supervisory, Ji, Hall editions and the History of the Southern Dynasties.
s0116.idiomatic: Deleted per the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions and the History of the Southern Dynasties.

s0117.literal: Comment: The Southern Supervisory edition also has the two characters "Yuan Jian"; alternatively deleting "them" yields "at Dongguan inflicted a great defeat on Yuan Jian," which also makes sense.
s0117.idiomatic: Note: the Southern Supervisory edition also reads Yuan Jian; deleting them gives at Dongguan inflicted a great defeat on Yuan Jian, which also works.

s0118.literal: Qi man Dongfang Guang held Suyu and sought surrender—On "Dongfang Guang": in the Comprehensive Mirror for Liang Emperor Yuan's Chengsheng years two and three it appears twice, both as "Dongfang Bai'e"; the same in the Northern Qi History biography of Duan Shao—it is suspected Bai'e was Guang's alias.
s0118.idiomatic: On Qi man Dongfang Guang holding Suyu and seeking surrender: the Comprehensive Mirror in Chengsheng years two and three of Emperor Yuan of Liang twice reads Dongfang Bai'e, as does the Northern Qi History biography of Duan Shao; Bai'e was probably Guang's alias.

s0119.literal: Following Zhang Zhaoda south to pacify Ouyang Xie—Comment: "da" was originally corrupt as "lian"; all editions are not corrupt; now corrected.
s0119.idiomatic: On following Zhang Zhaoda south to pacify Ouyang Xie: da was originally written lian; other editions are correct; emended.

s0120.literal: Military Affairs along the Yangzi of Xuzhou—Zhang Senkai
s0120.idiomatic: Military affairs along the Yangzi of Xuzhou—Zhang Senkai

s0122.literal: Says: "Above 'Xu' it is suspected there is the character 'south'; below it says 'Inspector of South Xuzhou,' so here it cannot merely say 'Xu.'"
s0122.idiomatic: He writes: "South probably belongs before Xu; since the text below says inspector of South Xuzhou, Xu alone cannot be right here."

s0124.literal: Xu Du as Administrator of Wu commandery—deleted according to Northern Supervisory and Hall editions.
s0124.idiomatic: On Xu Du as administrator of Wu commandery: deleted per the Northern Supervisory and Hall editions.

s0125.literal: The Founder executed Wang Sengbian—Hall edition textual verification says above "executed" the History of the Southern Dynasties has "plotted."
s0125.idiomatic: On the Founder executing Wang Sengbian: the Hall edition notes that the History of the Southern Dynasties reads plotted above executed.

s0126.idiomatic: Present opinion: plotted is the correct reading.

s0127.literal: Still ordered to recruit clan and follower kinsmen—Hall edition textual verification says "recruit" in the History of the Southern Dynasties reads "gather."
s0127.idiomatic: On still ordered to recruit clan and follower kinsmen: the Hall edition notes the History of the Southern Dynasties reads gather for recruit.

s0131.literal: Comment: "jun" in all editions is "commandery," showing this "jun" (lord) is corruption of commandery.
s0131.idiomatic: Note: in every edition jun is commandery, showing this jun (lord) is a corruption of commandery.

s0132.literal: Yet Shen Ke was already Supernumerary Scattered-Cavalry Regular Attendant and enfeoffed as county marquis; there is no reason he would again become a commandery chief minister.
s0132.idiomatic: Yet Shen Ke was already supernumerary scattered-cavalry regular attendant and enfeoffed as a county marquis; he could not logically have become a commandery chief minister again.

s0133.literal: Probably at that time Chen Baxian was Area Commander over Military Affairs of South Xuzhou, Grand General Who Campaigns North, Opener of the Mansion Equal to the Three Dukes, and Inspector of South Xuzhou; Ke was chief minister of his bureau.
s0133.idiomatic: Probably then Chen Baxian was commander of South Xuzhou armies, grand general who campaigns north, opener of the mansion equal to the three dukes, and inspector of South Xuzhou; Ke was chief minister of his staff.

s0134.literal: The Yuan Gui reading "prefecture bureau chief minister" is correct.
s0134.idiomatic: Yuan Gui's reading prefecture chief minister is correct.

s0135.literal: Ordered to lead troops in to take leave—Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions lack "leave"; History of the Southern Dynasties the same.
s0135.idiomatic: On ordered to lead troops in to take leave: the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions omit leave, as does the History of the Southern Dynasties.

s0136.literal: From Guangda year two to "changed to Protector General"—comment:
s0136.idiomatic: On from Guangda year two to changed to protector general—note:

s0138.literal: , Shen Ke's transfer to General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Jingzhou was in the eleventh month of Guangda year one; changed to Protector General in the eleventh month of Guangda year two.
s0138.idiomatic: , Shen Ke's promotion to general who pacifies the west and inspector of Jingzhou fell in the eleventh month of Guangda year one; his change to protector general in the eleventh month of Guangda year two.
